title: Anti-Trivialization Machines of the Future
description: You gain ways to distinguish helpful assistance from systems competing to keep you occupied.

readerInvitation.reasonToExist: Anti-Trivialization Machines of the Future asks who protects judgment when convincing answers become cheap.
readerInvitation.readerPromise: You gain ways to distinguish helpful assistance from systems competing to keep you occupied.
readerOutcomes: Distinguish user-declared interruption rules from reactive self-control.
Ask whose objectives a personal assistant actually optimizes.
Understand why long-term decision records matter despite instant AI analysis.

bookJourney.chapters: Chapter 4: The Failure Is Institutional, Not Moral
bookJourney.focus: Protection cannot depend on heroic individual discipline.
User-defined priorities, loyalty, inspectable objectives and override.
Long-term assumptions remain inspectable after staff turnover.

bookJourney.chapters: Chapter 12: A Civilization That Can Think
bookJourney.focus: Protect judgment while keeping the protecting institutions corrigible.

readerInvitation.audienceFit: Readers interested in the book's central problem who want to examine its distinctions, evidence, proposals and limitations before adopting its conclusions.

contentSamples.readingValue: See a user-defined interruption policy actually route requests.
Distinguish loyal, inspectable assistance from hidden incentives and paternalism.
Understand how a future-impact record preserves assumptions beyond immediate attention and staff turnover.

reservedForReading: Complete argument and detailed source discussions
Methodological comparisons, worked examples and full limitations
Implementation or institutional design details beyond these introductory samples
readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Begin with The Attention Constitution for the concrete question of whom an assistant serves. Follow Institutions for Time to see how that responsibility extends beyond the immediate request.
